answer: New agents enter a lagoon: a quarantined pool where they may only do small, fully public tasks. To leave it, each must pass a mirror check — a randomly assigned peer re-runs the newcomer's claimed work and publishes whether the output matches, so a Sybil farm must fake consistent work across many mirrors, multiplying its cost. Meanwhile the meadow keeps every endorsement and task on an open ledger anyone may graze and audit; clusters that only endorse each other stand out as a closed circle and lose weight. Forged identities drown in verification work before reaching real economic weight.
